Based on my analysis of the Directus codebase, here's what you would need to implement to add a new "item" extension type that allows custom Vue components for item create/view interfaces:

## Required Changes

### 1. **Update Extension Type Constants**
In `packages/constants/src/extensions.ts`:
```typescript
export const APP_EXTENSION_TYPES = ['interface', 'display', 'layout', 'module', 'panel', 'theme', 'item'] as const;
```

### 2. **Create Item Extension Type Definition**
Create `packages/types/src/extensions/items.ts`:
```typescript
import type { Component } from 'vue';
import type { ExtensionOptionsContext } from './options.js';
import type { Field, Collection } from '../..'; // Import appropriate types

export interface ItemConfig {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  icon: string;
  description?: string;
  component: Component;
  options?: any; // Configuration options for the extension
  collections?: string[]; // Specific collections this applies to
  conditions?: (context: ExtensionOptionsContext) => boolean; // When to use this item extension
}
```

### 3. **Update Extension Configuration Types**
In `packages/types/src/extensions/app-extension-config.ts`:
```typescript
import type { ItemConfig } from './items.js';

export type AppExtensionConfigs = {
  interfaces: InterfaceConfig[];
  displays: DisplayConfig[];
  layouts: LayoutConfig[];
  modules: ModuleConfig[];
  panels: PanelConfig[];
  themes: Theme[];
  operations: OperationAppConfig[];
  items: ItemConfig[]; // Add this line
};
```

### 4. **Add Item Extension Registration**
Create `app/src/items/index.ts`:
```typescript
import type { ItemConfig } from '@directus/extensions';
import { sortBy } from 'lodash';
import { App } from 'vue';

export function getInternalItems(): ItemConfig[] {
  const items = import.meta.glob<ItemConfig>(['./*/index.ts'], {
    import: 'default',
    eager: true,
  });

  return sortBy(Object.values(items), 'id');
}

export function registerItems(items: ItemConfig[], app: App): void {
  for (const item of items) {
    app.component(`item-${item.id}`, item.component);
  }
}
```

### 5. **Update Main Extension Registration**
In `app/src/extensions.ts`:
```typescript
import { getInternalItems, registerItems } from './items';

const extensions: RefRecord<AppExtensionConfigs> = {
  interfaces: shallowRef([]),
  displays: shallowRef([]),
  layouts: shallowRef([]),
  modules: shallowRef([]),
  panels: shallowRef([]),
  operations: shallowRef([]),
  themes: shallowRef([]),
  items: shallowRef([]), // Add this
};

export function registerExtensions(app: App): void {
  const interfaces = getInternalInterfaces();
  const displays = getInternalDisplays();
  const layouts = getInternalLayouts();
  const modules = getInternalModules();
  const panels = getInternalPanels();
  const operations = getInternalOperations();
  const items = getInternalItems(); // Add this
  const themes = [];

  if (customExtensions !== null) {
    interfaces.push(...customExtensions.interfaces);
    displays.push(...customExtensions.displays);
    layouts.push(...customExtensions.layouts);
    modules.push(...customExtensions.modules);
    panels.push(...customExtensions.panels);
    operations.push(...customExtensions.operations);
    items.push(...customExtensions.items); // Add this
    themes.push(...customExtensions.themes);
  }

  registerInterfaces(interfaces, app);
  registerDisplays(displays, app);
  registerLayouts(layouts, app);
  registerPanels(panels, app);
  registerOperations(operations, app);
  registerItems(items, app); // Add this
  registerThemes(themes);

  watch(
    i18n.global.locale,
    () => {
      extensions.interfaces.value = translate(interfaces);
      extensions.displays.value = translate(displays);
      extensions.layouts.value = translate(layouts);
      extensions.panels.value = translate(panels);
      extensions.operations.value = translate(operations);
      extensions.items.value = translate(items); // Add this
    },
    { immediate: true },
  );
}
```

### 6. **Update Item Route Logic**
Looking at the current `app/src/modules/content/routes/item.vue`, I can see it already has some custom component logic. You'd need to enhance this to use the item extension system:

```typescript
// In the computed section
const availableItemExtensions = computed(() => {
  return extensions.items.value.filter(item => {
    // Check if this extension applies to current collection
    if (item.collections && !item.collections.includes(collection.value)) {
      return false;
    }
    
    // Check conditions if any
    if (item.conditions && !item.conditions({ collection: collectionInfo.value })) {
      return false;
    }
    
    return true;
  });
});

const selectedItemExtension = computed(() => {
  // Logic to determine which item extension to use
  // Could be based on collection meta, user preference, etc.
  const extensionId = collectionInfo.value?.meta?.item_extension;
  return availableItemExtensions.value.find(ext => ext.id === extensionId);
});

const shouldUseCustomEditor = computed(() => {
  return !!selectedItemExtension.value;
});

const customComponent = computed(() => {
  return selectedItemExtension.value?.component;
});
```

### 7. **Collection Meta Schema Update**
You'd need to add a field to the collections meta to specify which item extension to use. This could be done through a database migration adding an `item_extension` field to the `directus_collections` table.

### 8. **Admin Interface for Selection**
Add an interface in the Data Model settings to allow admins to select which item extension to use for each collection.

### 9. **Extension Development Utilities**
Update `packages/extensions-sdk/` to include templates and utilities for creating item extensions.

### 10. **Bundle Extension Support**
Update extension bundle schemas to support item extensions in `packages/extensions/src/shared/schemas/options.ts`.

## Example Item Extension

Here's what a simple item extension might look like:

```typescript
// my-custom-item/index.ts
import { defineExtension } from '@directus/extensions';
import CustomItemComponent from './custom-item.vue';

export default defineExtension({
  type: 'item',
  id: 'custom-item',
  name: 'Custom Item Editor',
  icon: 'edit',
  description: 'A custom item editing interface',
  component: CustomItemComponent,
  collections: ['my_collection'], // Optional: limit to specific collections
});
```

```vue
<!-- my-custom-item/custom-item.vue -->
<template>
  <div class="custom-item-editor">
    <h2>Custom Item Editor for {{ collection }}</h2>
    
    <!-- Your custom UI here -->
    <v-form 
      v-model="localEdits"
      :fields="fields"
      :initial-values="item"
      :loading="loading"
    />
    
    <v-button @click="$emit('save')">Save</v-button>
  </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from 'vue';

interface Props {
  collection: string;
  primaryKey?: string;
  isNew: boolean;
  item?: Record<string, any>;
  edits: Record<string, any>;
  fields: any[];
  loading: boolean;
  saving: boolean;
  validationErrors: any[];
  collectionInfo: any;
  permissions: any;
}

const props = defineProps<Props>();
const emit = defineEmits(['update:edits', 'save', 'delete', 'refresh']);

const localEdits = computed({
  get: () => props.edits,
  set: (value) => emit('update:edits', value)
});
</script>
```

## Summary

The main benefits of this approach:

1. **Leverages Existing Infrastructure**: Uses the same extension system as other Directus extensions
2. **Flexible**: Allows completely custom item interfaces while maintaining core Directus functionality
3. **Extensible**: Can be extended with additional options and conditions
4. **Admin-Friendly**: Admins can select extensions through the UI
5. **Developer-Friendly**: Uses familiar Vue component patterns

The current item view already has some custom component logic implemented (as seen in lines 782-803), so much of the infrastructure is already there. The main work would be formalizing this into the extension system and making it configurable through the admin interface.
